verses.text: Here's the main point of what we're saying: we have a high priest like this, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven.
He serves in the holy place, the true tent set up by the Lord, not by a human being.
Every high priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices. So this high priest also had to have something to offer.
If he were on earth, he wouldn't be a priest at all, since there are already priests who offer gifts according to the law.

They serve in a place that is only a copy and shadow of what's in heaven. Moses was warned by God before he built the tent: ‘Be sure to make everything according to the pattern you were shown on the mountain.’
But Jesus has received a ministry far greater than theirs, just as the covenant he mediates is better and rests on better promises.
If the first covenant had been faultless, there would have been no need to look for a second.
But God found fault with the people and said: ‘The days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the people of Israel and Judah.

It won't be like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I took them by the hand and led them out of Egypt. They didn't remain faithful to my covenant, so I turned away from them, says the Lord.

This is the covenant I will make with the people of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
No longer will each person teach a neighbor or a brother and say, ‘Know the Lord.’ Everyone, from the least to the greatest, will know me.
I will forgive their wrongdoing and never again remember their sins.’
By calling it a new covenant, God has made the first one outdated. And what is outdated and growing old will soon disappear.
